summary: Review-required audit trail for the live product-key cleanup card. The app already exposes the slmgr-backed action and repo docs map the tweak id to the same cleanup flow, but the card still lives only in the first-party provider and has not yet been promoted into the validated research-provider surface.

setting.name: Remove Product Key from Registry
setting.casual_explanation: This runs the Windows licensing cleanup command that removes the product key from the registry so malware or local snooping has less to steal.
setting.why_people_change_it: People use it when they want to scrub the locally stored product key after activation and accept that restoring it later requires manual re-entry or reactivation steps.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: It can reduce local key exposure, but it is still a one-shot maintenance action with no automatic rollback. This record documents the shipped app behavior without yet promoting it into the validated research surface.
setting.professional_notes: The live app models this card as a command tweak that detects with cscript slmgr.vbs /dli and applies with cscript slmgr.vbs /cpky. Repo cleanup docs and tweak provenance both map the tweak id to that exact product-key cleanup action. The record stays review-required until command-backed cleanup cards move through the normal research-provider promotion path.

blocking_issues: The card has not yet been promoted into the research-provider surface.

decision.promotion_disposition_reason: Closed as rejected for research-provider promotion because the live action is one-shot, destructive, high-risk, reboot-sensitive, or lacks a rollback story suitable for a validated tweak card.
decision.promotion_reopen_criteria: Reopen only if the app gains a verified rollback/snapshot contract and dedicated validation proof for the exact action.
